doc.citation: Di Pasquo, M.M. and Noetinger, S. (2008). First record of Early Devonian (Lochkovian) flora from the Santa Rosa Formation - Alarache, Southern Bolivia. Geologica Acta, 6(2), 191–210.
doc.comment: Two newly studied assemblages are reported, three metres apart. Their Lochkovian age is based on spores and constrained by absences of index taxa. The formal description uses Acinosporites macgregorii, whereas assemblage lists and captions use mcgregorii; printed list spellings are retained below. Caption variants referring to the same taxon are consolidated. Exclusively in situ spores and literature comparisons are excluded. Earlier records discussed include McGregor (1984), Late Silurian and Devonian spores from Bolivia, and Melo (2005b), cited for spores from the same locality; reuse of their material is not stated.

items.locality: Angosto de Alarache, near Tarija city, Tarija Department
items.depth_or_level: Lower plant-bearing interval; laminated and massive siltstones in heterolithic facies; three metres below assemblage 2. BAFC-Pb 16988, 16989 and BAFC-Pl 1632.
items.age_basis_detail: Assigned the same age as assemblage 2, three metres above. Assemblage 2 is dated by Dictyotriletes emsiensis, Apiculiretusispora plicata, Retusotriletes albarinii and Retusotriletes maculatus, with absence of other index taxa restricting the age up to the Late not latest Lochkovian. Correlated with the lower Ems Zone of the Amazon Basin and MN Zone of Western Europe.
items.setting_as_reported: marginal to low energy marine palaeoenvironments
items.n_samples: Two plant-bearing blocks, BAFC-Pb 16988 and 16989, and pelitic sample BAFC-Pl 1632
items.notes: Reported collectively across successive plant-bearing bedding planes. Phytodebris constitutes around 80% of the residue; trilete spores constitute 85% of palynomorphs and cryptospores 14%. Poorly preserved chitinozoans and aquatic algae also occur. Short-distance transport and paraautochthonous to allochthonous deposition are interpreted; stratigraphic reworking is not reported. Punctatisporites spp. is illustrated as Punctatisporites sp. in Fig. 7G. The tentative Dibolisporites identification and unidentified tetrad are added from Fig. 7. Retusotriletes albarinii includes a corroded specimen. The caption-only tentative Punctatisporites and Apiculiretusispora identifications associated with isolated sporangia are excluded as in situ records. Coordinates are printed without hemisphere designations.

items.locality: Angosto de Alarache, near Tarija city, Tarija Department
items.depth_or_level: Upper dark grey claystone bed above a sandstone bed with current structures; three metres above assemblage 1. BAFC-Pl 1631.
items.age_basis_detail: Based on Dictyotriletes emsiensis, Apiculiretusispora plicata, Retusotriletes cf. avonensis (= R. albarinii n. sp.) and Retusotriletes maculatus. Absence of Urochitina loboi and other index taxa restricts the age up to the Late not latest Lochkovian. Correlated with the lower Ems Zone of the Amazon Basin and MN Zone of Western Europe.
items.setting_as_reported: marginal to low energy marine palaeoenvironments
items.notes: Phytodebris constitutes 70%; trilete spores dominate the palynomorph assemblage. Cryptospores include tetrads, dyads and uncertain single forms. Ambitisporites specimens are described as corroded, without a claim of reworking. Fig. 9D prints Apiculiretusipora sp.; this is consolidated with Apiculiretusispora sp. illustrated in Fig. 9G. Fig. 9F identifies Dictyotriletes emsiensis as a morphon. Fig. 8V is captioned Cryptospore and the same specimen is captioned ?Cryptospore in Fig. 9T. The possible sphaeromorph ?Leiosphaeridia in Fig. 9I is excluded from spore occurrences. Coordinates are printed without hemisphere designations.
